item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's Monte dei Paschi di Siena (BMPS.MI) said on Thursday it has received approval from the European Central Bank to merge recently acquired peer Mediobanca (MDBI.MI) into the group.

item.title: La presentadora Maria Bartiromo deja Fox News Media
item.description: Fox News Media anunció el jueves que su veterana presentadora de noticias económicas, Maria Bartiromo, dejaba la cadena tras más de una década en la compañía.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: Fox News Media anunció el jueves que su veterana presentadora de noticias económicas, Maria Bartiromo, dejaba la cadena tras más de una década en la compañía. La empresa no ha dado ninguna razón para su salida, que, según ha indicado, tiene efecto inmediato. "Agradecemos a Maria su trabajo durante los últimos doce años y medio y le deseamos lo mejor en esta nueva etapa", dijo Fox News Media en un comunicado. Bartiromo, que apareció por última vez en pantalla el 9 de agosto, no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. Bartiromo presentaba un programa matutino diario, "Mornings with Maria", en Fox Business, así como un programa los viernes por la noche, "Maria Bartiromo's Wall Street", y un programa los domingos por la mañana, "Sunday Morning Futures". La presentadora de televisión consiguió una de las primeras entrevistas con el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, tras su salida de la Casa Blanca en 2021. Su repentina salida se anuncia tras la dimisión de Karoline Leavitt como secretaria de prensa de la Casa Blanca el mes pasado, aunque el vicepresidente JD Vance, al ser preguntado el jueves sobre si Bartiromo sería la próxima secretaria de prensa, respondió a los periodistas: "No, no lo creo". "Acabo de ver la noticia, literalmente, al salir", dijo Vance en la sala de prensa de la Casa Blanca. "Me encanta Maria. Creo que es una persona increíble, con un talento extraordinario. No me meto en los dramas de personal de las cadenas de televisión". Bartiromo se incorporó a Fox News en 2013 tras dos décadas en la cadena rival CNBC, donde se convirtió en la primera periodista en informar en directo a diario desde el parqué de la Bolsa de Nueva York.

item.title: Blue Jays surge past fellow wild-card contending Guardians
item.description: Nathan Lukes delivered the go-ahead, two-run double in a four-run fifth inning and rookie Brett Bateman had three hits as the visiting Toronto Blue Jays beat the Cleveland Guardians 6-3 on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nathan Lukes delivered the go-ahead, two-run double in a four-run fifth inning and rookie Brett Bateman had three hits as the visiting Toronto Blue Jays beat the Cleveland Guardians 6-3 on Thursday afternoon. Toronto (70-71) scored five consecutive runs to claim the rubber match of the three-game series between American League postseason contenders. Cleveland (70-70) holds the final wild-card spot, but the Blue Jays are just 1/2 game behind. Lukes' two-run liner to right-center chased Guardians starter Tanner Bibee (5-15), who took over the major league lead in losses. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. and Jesus Sanchez followed with RBIs against Colin Holderman as Toronto seized a 5-1 advantage. Spencer Miles (6-2) earned the win with 1 1/3 innings of scoreless relief. Closer Louis Varland brought the tying run to the plate in the ninth before striking out Angel Genao and picking up his 32nd save in 33 opportunities. Cleveland's Austin Hedges had a two-run single in the bottom of the fifth off Mason Fluharty, scoring Jo Adell and Genao to close the deficit to 5-3. But Miles and fellow right-handers Tyler Rogers and Varland shut the door the rest of the way. Jose Soriano worked the first 4 2/3 innings for the Blue Jays and smacked his glove in frustration when he was pulled one out shy of qualifying for the win. The right-hander gave up three runs on six hits, walking three with a pair of strikeouts. Bibee tied his career high with five walks over four-plus innings, being charged with five runs on four hits. The righty struck out four, falling to 1-6 in eight starts since July 25, and hasn't won at home since July 20. Ernie Clement singled in Josh Smith in the ninth with an insurance run for Toronto. The run was given up by Carlos Hernandez, the seventh Guardians pitcher of the day. Cleveland got on the board in the third when Genao singled in Adell. The Blue Jays answered in the fourth on Sean Keys' RBI single that plated Guerrero, who walked after a foul ball dropped between catcher Hedges and third baseman Genao earlier in the at-bat. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brasil ameaça retaliar UE se negociações sobre embargo a carnes não avançarem
item.description: O governo brasileiro pode recorrer a medidas de reciprocidade contra embargo europeu a produtos de origem animal do Brasil, de acordo com um comunicado conjunto dos ministérios de Agricultura e de Relações Exteriores nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O governo brasileiro pode recorrer a medidas de reciprocidade contra embargo europeu a produtos de origem animal do Brasil, de acordo com um comunicado conjunto dos ministérios de Agricultura e de Relações Exteriores nesta quinta-feira. A retaliação ocorreria caso as negociações com os europeus não tenham uma solução satisfatória, observou a nota. O comunicado foi publicado no dia em que começou a vigorar um [USN:L1N44V0R6 TEXT:"embargo"] da União Europeia a produtos de origem animal do Brasil, atingindo exportações avaliadas em US$1,84 bilhão em 2025, principalmente carnes. A suspensão das importações desses produtos brasileiros acontece, segundo a Comissão Europeia, porque o bloco europeu ainda busca garantias do Estado sobre a ausência de substâncias antimicrobianas no processo produtivo no país. A nota do governo brasileiro expressa "profunda preocupação" com o início da implementação das restrições impostas pela União Europeia. Diz ainda que o governo brasileiro mantém contato contínuo com a União Europeia e com os setores produtivos envolvidos, com vistas à continuidade dos fluxos comerciais, mas faz uma ameaça de retaliação. "Caso as tratativas não conduzam tempestivamente a uma solução satisfatória, o governo brasileiro reserva-se o direito de recorrer aos instrumentos cabíveis para assegurar condições equilibradas de comércio, inclusive às medidas de reciprocidade previstas no ordenamento jurídico nacional, bem como aos mecanismos pertinentes previstos no Acordo Mercosul-União Europeia e no sistema multilateral de comércio", afirmou. No comunicado o governo brasileiro acrescenta que os produtos afetados pelas novas restrições foram objeto de cotas e reduções tarifárias no âmbito do Acordo Mercosul-União Europeia, e que a "exclusão desses produtos do mercado europeu anula uma parte importante dos ganhos obtidos pelo Brasil nas negociações".

item.title: Brazil warns of reciprocal measures against EU if talks to lift meat ban stall
item.description: The Brazilian government said on Thursday it could take reciprocal measures against the European Union in case negotiations to reverse the bloc's ban on animal products from the South American nation do not lead to "a satisfactory outcome."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Brazilian government said on Thursday it could take reciprocal measures against the European Union in case negotiations to reverse the bloc's [USN:L8N44T0ZE TEXT:"ban on animal products"] from the South American nation do not lead to "a satisfactory outcome." In a statement signed by the ministries of agriculture and foreign affairs, Brazil expressed concerns over the ban, which took effect on Thursday as the European bloc seeks guarantees that prohibited antimicrobial substances are not used in production.

item.title: TRADING DAY Waller cools Fed hike hoopla
item.description: Remarks from Fed Governor Christopher Waller that he is inclined to hold interest rates steady later this month sparked a strong stock market rally and dragged bond yields lower on Thursday, while the Japanese yen clocked its strongest New York trading day close since the U.S.-Iran war started.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: Remarks from Fed Governor Christopher Waller that he is inclined to hold interest rates steady later this month sparked a strong [USN:L4N44V0PK TEXT:"stock market rally"] and dragged bond yields lower on Thursday, while the Japanese [USN:L1N44V00I TEXT:"yen"] clocked its strongest New York trading day close since the U.S.-Iran war started. In [USN:L6N44U0ZU TEXT:"my column today"], I look at how the ownership structure - and risk profile - of the U.S. government bond market has changed over the years. Remember when China was considered the biggest threat to Treasuries? Paradoxically, Beijing's large footprint was a source of stability, and it has been replaced by flightier, more leveraged "fast money" investors. If you have more time to read, here are a few articles I recommend to help you make sense of what happened in markets today. [USN:S0N4490CF TEXT:"Fed's Waller channels his inner John Lennon with a plea to 'give disinflation a chance'"] [USN:L1N44T0Z5 TEXT:"Bond selloff is likely amplified by obscure economic rate"] [USN:L1N44U12K TEXT:"US labor market remains stable; services input price rises point to elevated inflation"] [USN:L6N44U14E TEXT:"US hyperscalers' euro thirst — lifeblood or vampire?: Mike Dolan"] [USN:L4N44V0WH TEXT:"Nvidia to buy Hugging Face for $13 billion in big bet on open AI models"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia muted, Europe and UK up 0.5% or more, US leaps: Main three indices all +1% or more. SECTORS/SHARES: Nine sectors on the S&P 500 rise, two fall. Consumer discretionaries, financials +1.6%. Energy -0.7%. Robinhood +16%, Palantir +8%, Oracle +6%. FX: [USN:L1N44V00I TEXT:"Dollar/yen"] tumbles 2% to as low as 155.30. Dollar index -0.8%. Bitcoin +5% back above $80,000. BONDS: Yields fall globally, come off multi-year highs. 10-year gilt yield has biggest fall in a month; U.S. yields -5 bps at short end, curve bear steepens. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L6N44V0ZE TEXT:"Oil"] up again on U.S.-Iran escalation , now +45% y/y. Average U.S. [USN:L6N44V1CG TEXT:"diesel hits record"] $5.82/gallon. [USN:L4N44V00N TEXT:"Gold"] +2%, other precious metals +5%. Today's Talking Points: This-ism, that-ism It's now a coin flip whether the Fed keeps rates on hold later this month or delivers the first hike in three years, according to rates futures pricing. That's the state of play after Fed Governor Christopher Waller's speech and Q&A with Reuters on Thursday. "Give disinflation a chance," the influential FOMC policymaker pleaded, although he also said he would raise rates if inflation comes in hotter than expected. In many ways, this is getting a bit ridiculous, as it now looks like a monumental policy decision could hinge on one data point, August CPI. Would a month-on-month rise of 0.26% signal a hike, but 0.24% signal no change? Similarly, would 0.26% or 0.34% prints be viewed equally? Also, didn't Chair Warsh say only last week that "trends matter most", and the Fed should not rely on "isolated data points"? And who said less than two months ago that "sternly staring at inflation until it melts before our withering gaze is not an option"? Cash splash Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, on Thursday announced one of its biggest deals, a $13 billion purchase of popular developer platform [USN:L4N44V0WH TEXT:"Hugging Face"]. It's a bet that support for open AI models will drive future demand even as its biggest customers develop their own chips to reduce reliance on the semiconductor giant. This follows the purchase of a $3.5 billion stake in Taiwan's MediaTek, and up to for OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease. Nvidia is trying to extend its influence and reach across the AI complex as widely as it can. But the more it does so, the more it will face accusations of [USN:L1N44010Z TEXT:""circular financing""] and an unsustainable reliance on revenue from customers it is supporting via financial tie-ups. Investors are shrugging it off for now - after sliding 20% earlier this summer, Nvidia shares are up 20% in the past month. The yen also rises Is Tokyo - and Washington, for that matter - finally turning the yen's tide? The Japanese currency soared 2% on Thursday, to its strongest New York session closing level since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February. The rally [USN:SPN43U00J TEXT:"didn't have"] the helping hand of official intervention behind it either, seemingly, making it all the more remarkable. Traders are betting heavily on a BOJ rate hike later this month, and another 50 bps of tightening by April. It would appear Japanese and U.S. policymakers are not happy with dollar/yen above 160.00, and a more hawkish BOJ would help maintain that 'line in the sand' intact. But will monetary tightening be enough on its own? Japan's bond market suggests fiscal policy will have to do some of the heavy lifting too, and that seems far less of a guarantee right now. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: Petróleo fecha misto entre riscos geopolíticos no Oriente Médio e aceno de Putin por paz
item.description: Os preços do petróleo fecharam sem direção comum nesta quinta-feira, apoiados pelos ataques dos Estados Unidos ao Irã e pelas renovadas ameaças israelenses contra Teerã, que reavivaram as preocupações com a interrupção do fornecimento no Oriente Médio, mas pressionados por comentários do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, sinalizando abertura para negociações de paz.
item.dc:creator: Nicole Jao
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo fecharam sem direção comum nesta quinta-feira, apoiados pelos ataques dos Estados Unidos ao Irã e pelas renovadas ameaças israelenses contra Teerã, que reavivaram as preocupações com a interrupção do fornecimento no Oriente Médio, mas pressionados por comentários do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, sinalizando abertura para negociações de paz. Os contratos futuros do petróleo Brent fecharam em queda de 0,12%, a US$95,52 por barril, enquanto os contratos futuros do petróleo West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dos EUA subiram 0,32%, para US$91,30. Ambos os contratos atingiram máximas de seis semanas no início do pregão. O ministro da Saúde do Irã informou que 18 pessoas morreram e 108 ficaram feridas nos ataques dos EUA realizados na noite de terça-feira em todo o Irã. O Crescente Vermelho Iraniano informou que quatro pessoas morreram e 67 ficaram feridas durante uma cerimônia de casamento perto da costa do Estreito de Ormuz. Três pilotos do Exército iraniano morreram nos ataques dos EUA, informou a agência de notícias semioficial Tasnim. Os ataques representaram o confronto mais substancial entre os EUA e o Irã desde julho. A guerra, que começou com ataques dos EUA e de Israel no final de fevereiro, está em seu sétimo mês. O vice-presidente JD Vance disse aos repórteres nesta quinta-feira que os EUA não planejam manter negociações com o Irã, a menos que Teerã pare de atacar navios comerciais no Estreito de Ormuz. “O mercado ficará atento para saber se o ataque dos EUA no início desta semana foi um evento isolado ou não”, disse o analista do UBS, Giovanni Staunovo. O ministro da Defesa de Israel, Israel Katz, reiterou as advertências de que Israel “paralisaria” a infraestrutura militar e civil do Irã, incluindo instalações de energia, caso Teerã lançasse ataques contra o país. O analista do Saxo Bank, Ole Hansen, disse que os comentários de Katz ajudaram a impulsionar os preços do petróleo para cima. Comentários do presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, indicando abertura para negociações de paz com a Ucrânia poderiam ajudar a amenizar as preocupações com interrupções no abastecimento de combustível russo, caso os ataques a refinarias diminuam e a produção se normalize — um fator que pressionou os preços nesta quinta-feira, disse Phil Flynn, do Price Futures Group. Putin afirmou nesta quinta-feira que havia uma chance de se chegar a um acordo para encerrar a guerra na Ucrânia. Falando em um fórum econômico no Extremo Oriente da Rússia, ele disse que vários países, incluindo os EUA e a China, estavam prontos para apoiar um acordo de paz.

item.title: Astros pitching holds down White Sox in series-clinching win
item.description: Daulton Varsho ripped a two-run triple and scored as part of a four-run third inning, fueling the host Houston Astros to a 6-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox on Thursday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Daulton Varsho ripped a two-run triple and scored as part of a four-run third inning, fueling the host Houston Astros to a 6-2 victory over the Chicago White Sox on Thursday afternoon. The Astros took three-of-four in the series and five-of-seven from Chicago this season. Jose Altuve belted a two-run homer in the first inning and Isaac Paredes and Christian Walker each drove in a run for the Astros (72-69), who have won six of their last eight games. The offense was more than enough for Hunter Brown (5-3), who defeated the White Sox for the second time this season and improved to 6-0 in six career starts versus the club. He allowed two runs on six hits and struck out seven batters in six innings. Bennett Sousa and Bryan Abreu each struck out a batter and retired the side in order to bridge the gap to AJ Blubaugh, who recorded his 10th consecutive scoreless appearance. Chicago's Jake Rogers and Sam Antonacci each had an RBI single in the second inning. Miguel Vargas and Chase Meidroth each had two of the seven singles for the White Sox (73-67), who have lost four of their last five games. Paredes ripped an RBI double off the wall in left field to give Houston a 3-2 lead in the third inning. Varsho stepped up two batters later and plated a pair of runs after his blast off Luis Castillo (4-11) caromed off the wall in right-center field. Varsho didn't stay on third base for long, as he trotted home on Walker's single to center field to boost his team's advantage to 6-2. Castillo permitted six runs on six hits in four innings. Paredes worked a 10-pitch walk with two outs in the first inning before Altuve deposited a 0-1 fastball from Castillo over the wall in left field to open the scoring. Altuve's homer was his 15th of the season. The White Sox forged a 2-2 tie after Rogers' infield single plated Colson Montgomery and Antonacci's RBI single to left field scored Tristan Peters. --Field Level Media

item.title: Syria begins destroying Assad-era chemical weapons
item.description: Syria says it destroys recovered Assad-era chemical weapons materials and prepares the first court hearing for suspects linked to the programme.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Syria begins destroying Assad-era chemical weapons

Syria says it destroys recovered Assad-era chemical weapons materials and prepares the first court hearing for suspects linked to the programme.

BEIRUT: Syria has begun destroying the remnants of a clandestine Assad-era chemical weapons program that it recovered in May, the first such destruction in a decade, a Syrian envoy and a UN representative said on Thursday (Sep 3). Reuters reported in May that Syria's new leadership had located remnants of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's chemical weapons program, including raw materials and munitions similar to those used in deadly gas attacks during the country's civil war.  Izumi Nakamitsu, the United Nations High Representative for Disarmament Affairs, told a Security Council briefing on Thursday that for the first time since 2014, the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons had verified the destruction of chemical munitions in Syria.  Following the May finding, Syria had found "one additional chemical weapons production facility, a newly discovered chemical used in the production of nerve agents, and empty chemical munitions. It also declared two chemical weapons storage facilities where the newly discovered facilities were being stored," Nakamitsu said.  "PROTECTING THE WORLD AND THE REGION"

Last month, the OPCW deployed a team to Syria to verify the destruction of category three chemical weapons, referring to unfilled munitions and other equipment used to release chemical weapons. She said the team verified "the irreversible destruction of 42 aerial bombs" as part of that mission. Syria's ambassador to the UN, Ibrahim Olabi, told the council that Syria was "protecting the world and the region through such work". But he heavily criticised Israel, saying that repeated Israeli attacks had impeded some search and destruction operations, and exposed the Syrian teams at work to risk.  "We cannot safeguard the security of the region if our security is exposed to attacks at the hands of Israel, and they are flouting the security of the region at large, and they are breaching the conventions and treaties we have talked about," said Olabi, whose Arabic remarks were translated at the council.  The Israeli military did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Olabi said Syria was preparing to hold the first court hearing of people suspected of involvement in the chemical weapons programme. Syrian authorities earlier this year took 18 suspects into custody for alleged involvement in Assad's chemical weapons program, including high-level military, political and technical officials.

item.title: Tunisian Cassation Court upholds long sentences for opposition members
item.description: Tunisia's Cassation Court on Thursday upheld prison sentences of up to 45 years imposed on opposition leaders, lawyers and businessmen on charges of conspiracy, their lawyers and families told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tunisia's Cassation Court on Thursday upheld prison sentences of up to 45 years imposed on opposition leaders, lawyers and businessmen on charges of conspiracy, their lawyers and families told Reuters. The opposition said the ruling, which is the final stage of the three-year legal proceedings and cannot be appealed, reinforces President Kais Saied’s authoritarian rule. Forty people were charged with conspiring to overthrow the president in one of Tunisia’s largest recent political prosecutions. Twenty fled abroad and were sentenced in absentia. “The ruling confirms that the judiciary is not independent,” said lawyer Haifa Chebbi, daughter of prominent opposition figure and National Salvation Front leader Nejib Chebbi, who was sentenced to 12 years. "Opponents entered prison by political decision and will leave when Saied falls,” she said. Saied has said the judiciary remains independent and that he would not become a dictator. In 2023, when most of the defendants were arrested, he said the politicians were "traitors and terrorists" and that judges who would acquit them were their accomplices. Tunisia's justice minister has said the defendants tried to destabilise the country and overthrow Saied. Rights groups say Saied has controlled the judiciary since suspending parliament and seizing extraordinary powers in 2021, ruling by decree, dissolving the independent Supreme Judicial Council and sacking dozens of judges in 2022. Prominent opposition figures Ghazi Chaouachi, Issam Chebbi, Jawhar Ben Mbarek and Ridha Belhaj were sentenced to 20 years in prison, while politician Noureddine Bhiri received 10 years.

item.title: Peso mexicano y bolsa avanzan previo a datos laborales EEUU, impulsan comentarios Waller
item.description: El peso mexicano y la bolsa avanzaron el jueves, un día antes de un esperado informe de nóminas no agrícolas y la tasa de desempleo de Estados Unidos, mientras comentarios de Christopher Waller reforzaron las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal mantenga sin cambios los tipos de interés.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano y la bolsa avanzaron el jueves, un día antes de un esperado informe de nóminas no agrícolas y la tasa de desempleo de Estados Unidos, mientras comentarios de [USN:L6N44V0YC TEXT:"Christopher Waller"] reforzaron las expectativas de que la Reserva Federal mantenga sin cambios los tipos de interés. El gobernador del banco central estadounidense dijo que si se confirman que las presiones inflacionarias se están moderando podría inclinarse por dejar nuevamente los tasas en 3.50%-3.75% en su próxima decisión, un mensaje que moderó las expectativas de mayores costos de financiamiento en Estados Unidos. * La moneda doméstica cotizaba en 16.9216 unidades por dólar en la recta final de los negocios, con una ganancia de 0.25%. El movimiento acompañó a un declive global de la [USN:L1N44V0UV TEXT:"divisa estadounidense"] y un desempeño mixto de los [USN:L6N44V1C6 TEXT:"precios del petróleo"]. * "Desde mi perspectiva, es probable que el tipo de cambio se mantenga cotizando en un rango defensivo entre los 16.85 y 17.05, con la mirada enteramente puesta en el reporte oficial de nóminas no agrícolas de Estados Unidos de mañana", dijo Felipe Mendoza, analista de mercados de la firma EBC Financial Group. * El reporte será relevante para confirmar si el mercado laboral estadounidense conserva la resiliencia que ha llevado a la Fed a mantener sin cambios las tasas de interés desde diciembre. Las cifras ayudarán a calibrar el margen del banco central para extender la pausa monetaria, como planteó Waller. * Por la mañana se dio a conocer que las solicitudes semanales de [USN:L6N44V0XI TEXT:"subsidio por desempleo"] en Estados Unidos aumentaron ligeramente, sin apuntar a un deterioro relevante del mercado laboral hacia finales de agosto. * En México, la [USN:AQN2MHX14 TEXT:"confianza del consumidor"] mejoró en agosto por tercer mes consecutivo y alcanzó su mejor nivel desde agosto de 2025. El dato tuvo un impacto limitado sobre el mercado cambiario. * En la plaza accionaria, el índice S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) subió 0.85% a 65,436.16 puntos, su segunda jornada consecutiva de ganancias, apoyado por un avance de [USN:L1N44V0VN TEXT:"Wall Street"] y un mayor apetito por activos de riesgo. * Los títulos del minero Industrias Peñoles (PEOLES.MX) encabezaron las alzas, con un 3.72% más a 940.73 pesos. Los papeles del conglomerado Grupo Carso (GCARSOA1.MX) , del magnate Carlos Slim, aumentaron 3.67% a 143.29 pesos. * En cuanto a los bonos gubernamentales de largo plazo, el rendimiento a 10 años descendió dos puntos base a 9.28%, mientras que el del plazo a 20 años bajó uno puntos base a 9.77%.

item.title: Maria Bartiromo departs Fox News Media
item.description: Fox News Media said on Thursday it was parting ways with its longtime business anchor Maria Bartiromo after more than a decade with the company.
item.dc:creator: Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: Fox News Media said on Thursday it was parting ways with its longtime business anchor Maria Bartiromo after more than a decade with the company. The company gave no reason for her departure, which it said was effective immediately. "We thank Maria for her work over the last 12-1/2 years and wish her all the best on her next chapter," Fox News Media said in a statement. Bartiromo was last on the air on August 9. She did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Bartiromo was host of a daily morning show, "Mornings with Maria," on Fox Business, as well as a Friday evening show, "Maria Bartiromo’s Wall Street" and a Sunday morning program, "Sunday Morning Futures." She secured one of the first media interviews with U.S. President Donald Trump after he left the White House in 2021. Her sudden exit follows Karoline Leavitt's [USN:FWN4491F6 TEXT:"departure"] from the White House press secretary role last month, although Vice President JD Vance, asked on Thursday whether Bartiromo would be the next press secretary, told reporters: "No, I don't think so." "I just saw the news literally as I walked out," Vance said in the White House briefing room. "I love Maria. I think she's an amazing person, amazing talent. I don't get involved in the personal drama of media stations." Bartiromo [USN:L2N0J3272 TEXT:"joined"] Fox News in 2013 after two decades at rival CNBC, where she became the first journalist to report live daily from the floor of the New York Stock Exchange. She was among Fox hosts named in defamation litigation over the network's airing of [USN:L1N35723K TEXT:"false claims"] that voting technology companies helped to rig the 2020 U.S. presidential election, which Democrat Joe Biden won. Fox agreed in 2023 to pay Dominion Voting Systems [USN:L1N36K27J TEXT:"$787.5 million"] to settle one of the lawsuits, while Smartmatic's separate case against the network is still pending.

item.title: Williams sisters return to Grand Slam while Pegula, Shelton face tough tests at US Open
item.description: The U.S. Open singles draw reaches the third round on Friday, with top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz among those in action alongside home hopes Jessica Pegula and Ben Shelton.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Open singles draw reaches the third round on Friday, with top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz among those in action alongside home hopes Jessica Pegula and Ben Shelton. Women's doubles competition also continues at Flushing Meadows, where Serena and Venus Williams will team up at a Grand Slam for the first time in four years. TOP WOMEN'S MATCH: JESSICA PEGULA V LEYLAH FERNANDEZ Third seed Jessica Pegula, the 2024 U.S. Open runner-up, has reached the third round without dropping a set, winning both her matches comfortably and yet to face a break point. The 32-year-old American has been serving with authority in New York, using her accuracy and consistency to dictate points and limit opportunities for her opponents. Her next test comes against 23-year-old Leylah Fernandez, the 2021 runner-up, who has shown signs of rediscovering her best form in New York after a difficult Grand Slam season, advancing with victories over Mananchaya Sawangkaew and Zhang Shuai. "Leylah is really tough to play against. Being a lefty is always tricky," Pegula told reporters on Wednesday. "She's really aggressive. She changes the direction of the ball really well, hits a lot of good angles and is a good returner." Pegula leads the head-to-head 3-1 and won their most recent meeting in Miami earlier this year, but Fernandez's aggressive returning and proven record at Flushing Meadows should ensure a stern examination for the American. TOP MEN'S MATCH: BEN SHELTON V DENIS SHAPOVALOV Ben Shelton will look to extend his U.S. Open campaign when the eighth-seeded American faces Canada's Denis Shapovalov in a blockbuster third-round clash. The 23-year-old came through a four-set battle with Hubert Hurkacz to reach the third round in New York for the third successive year. Standing in his way is former U.S. Open quarter-finalist Shapovalov, who has dropped only one set through two rounds and arrives in encouraging form after reaching the Los Cabos final. The Canadian has impressed at Flushing Meadows by keeping his error count under control while using his aggressive game to dictate points, but he faces a difficult challenge against fellow left-hander Shelton. Shelton holds a 4-0 record against Shapovalov, although their meetings have rarely been straightforward. Their Wimbledon clash in 2024 went the distance, while the Canadian took the opening set before Shelton battled back to win their Dallas semi-final earlier this year. Their most recent meeting came in Dallas in February, where Shelton's victory propelled him towards the title. While Shapovalov has the firepower to trouble any opponent, Shelton's powerful serve and greater consistency from the baseline could give the American the edge. WILLIAMS SISTERS RETURN Two-time U.S. Open doubles champions Serena and Venus Williams will reunite at a Grand Slam for the first time since 2022 when they face 14th seeds Chan Hao-Ching and Maya Joint in the first round on Friday. Serena, 44, returned to doubles competition in June after an absence of nearly four years, partnering Canadian Victoria Mboko at Queen's Club and Karolina Muchova in Berlin before making her singles comeback at Wimbledon. The sisters had also planned to compete together at the All England Club before Serena's knee injury forced their withdrawal. They resumed their partnership in Cincinnati last month but suffered a first-round defeat. Venus, 46, reached the U.S. Open women's doubles quarter-finals alongside Fernandez last year and will hope for a similar run with her sister. They face a difficult opening test against Chan and Joint, who have enjoyed a strong start to their partnership, reaching the Memphis final, the second round in Toronto and the quarter-finals in Cincinnati. Joint also defeated Serena in the first round at Wimbledon earlier this summer, in the only singles match of the American's comeback so far. U.S. OPEN ORDER OF PLAY ON FRIDAY (prefix number denotes seeding): ARTHUR ASHE STADIUM (1530 GMT/1130 ET) 3-Jessica Pegula (U.S.) v 31-Leylah Fernandez (Canada) Yibing Wu (China) v 2-Carlos Alcaraz (Spain) Serena Williams (U.S.) & Venus Williams (U.S.) v 14-Chan Hao-Ching (China) and Maya Joint (Australia) 8-Ben Shelton (U.S.) v Denis Shapovalov (Canada) LOUIS ARMSTRONG STADIUM (1500 GMT/1100 ET) 1-Aryna Sabalenka (Belarus) v Kamilla Rakhimova (Uzbekistan) 15-Alexander Bublik (Kazakhstan) v 20-Tommy Paul (U.S.) 22-Valentin Vacherot (Monaco) v 11-Frances Tiafoe (U.S.) 9-Elina Svitolina (Ukraine) v Anna Kalinskaya (Russia)

item.title: SEC proposes reforms to political contribution rule for investment advisers
item.description: Wall Street's top regulator on Thursday proposed reforms to "pay-to-play" regulations intended to prevent investment advisers from winning business from public pension funds by making political contributions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's top regulator on Thursday proposed reforms to "pay-to-play" regulations intended to prevent investment advisers from winning business from public pension funds by making political contributions. Under President Donald Trump, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission has said the regulations create needless compliance burdens and are excessively restrictive for investment advisers.

item.title: Trump dice Reino Unido está "al borde del desastre", cita inmigración y energía como preocupantes
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó que el Reino Unido se encontraba "al borde del desastre" y expresó su preocupación, en una entrevista con GB News, por los elevados costos energéticos del país, las políticas de cero emisiones netas y el impacto de la inmigración masiva.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó que el Reino Unido se encontraba "al borde del desastre" y expresó su preocupación, en una entrevista con GB News, por los elevados costos energéticos del país, las políticas de cero emisiones netas y el impacto de la inmigración masiva. Las relaciones entre el Reino Unido y los Estados Unidos de Trump han sido turbulentas en los últimos años, pasando de los momentos álgidos de una visita de Estado llena de pompa a Londres en 2025 a fuertes críticas en diversos ámbitos de la política interior y exterior. En sus declaraciones del jueves, Trump reiteró su admiración y afecto por el rey Carlos, así como su amor por el Reino Unido como país, pero señaló que el Gobierno del primer ministro Andy Burnham tenía graves problemas que superar. "Su país está en apuros. Están al borde del desastre", afirmó. "Tienen un tremendo problema de inmigración y un tremendo problema energético. Sus precios de la energía son tres o cuatro veces más altos de lo que deberían ser". Trump, que califica el cambio climático de "engaño", ya había criticado anteriormente el abandono de los combustibles fósiles por parte de Gran Bretaña y había instado en repetidas ocasiones a los sucesivos líderes a explotar sus reservas de petróleo y gas del Mar del Norte. Burnham está sopesando si autorizar la puesta en marcha de dos grandes proyectos en el Mar del Norte, prometiendo un enfoque pragmático para la transición energética, pero reiterando la convicción de su Gobierno de que es necesario pasar a fuentes de electricidad limpias. Trump también afirmó que la inmigración estaba cambiando el panorama de Gran Bretaña. "Si no se detiene la afluencia de gente procedente de todo el mundo hacia tu país, no te quedará país", afirmó. La preocupación por la inmigración, centrada en las personas que llegan ilegalmente en pequeñas embarcaciones desde Europa continental, es uno de los temas más importantes para muchos votantes británicos y ha impulsado un aumento de la popularidad del partido de derecha Reform, de Nigel Farage. El Gobierno de Burnham ha reiterado los compromisos adquiridos por su predecesor, Keir Starmer, para poner fin a estas travesías. A principios de esta semana, afirmó que habían disminuido drásticamente y que las medidas dirigidas contra las embarcaciones y las bandas criminales que las organizan estaban dando sus frutos.

item.title: Adobe names Anil Chakravarthy as CEO, Narayen transitions to executive chair
item.description: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy as successor to long-time CEO Shantanu Narayen on Thursday, charging the insider with taking on a wave of new AI rivals threatening its design software dominance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Adobe (ADBE.O) named Anil Chakravarthy as successor to long-time CEO Shantanu Narayen on Thursday, charging the insider with taking on a wave of new AI rivals threatening its design software dominance. Narayen, who has served as CEO for over 18 years, will transition to executive chair, the company said. Adobe has been trying to reassure investors worried about disruptions to its business from potential improvements in AI technology. Its shares have fallen around 18% this year after declining over 21% in 2025. The Photoshop maker had [USN:L4N42J1OF TEXT:"raised"] its annual profit forecast in June, reflecting growing demand for its AI products and tools that are central to its strategy to hold on to its lead over challengers like Figma (FIG.N) and Canva. But the firm also announced the exit of finance chief Dan Durn the same month, adding to uncertainties till a permanent successor is named. It had [USN:L4N4001XH TEXT:"said"] in March that Narayen would step down as CEO once a successor was named, ending a tenure in which he helped turn flagship products such as Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro and InDesign into household names among creatives worldwide. Chakravarthy joined Adobe in January 2020 to lead its digital experience business and later took on responsibility for improving how customers interact with Adobe, as well as overseeing its global sales and customer-support teams. He was previously the chief executive of cloud data-management company Informatica for four years. Shares of Adobe dropped 1% in after-hours trading on Thursday.

item.title: Café arábica atinge nova mínima em 5 semanas; açúcar recua após máxima em 16 meses
item.description: Os contratos futuros do café arábica na bolsa ICE atingiram novas mínimas de cinco semanas nesta quinta-feira, devido às condições climáticas favoráveis e às perspectivas otimistas de oferta, enquanto o açúcar bruto recuou em relação às máximas de 16 meses registradas na sessão anterior.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do café arábica na bolsa ICE atingiram novas mínimas de cinco semanas nesta quinta-feira, devido às condições climáticas favoráveis e às perspectivas otimistas de oferta, enquanto o açúcar bruto recuou em relação às máximas de 16 meses registradas na sessão anterior. CAFÉ * Os contratos futuros de café arábica fecharam em queda de 2,75 centavos, ou 0,9%, a US$2,9535 por libra-peso, após atingirem uma nova mínima de cinco semanas de US$2,8975. * Uma recuperação nas exportações do Brasil, principal produtor, está ajudando a aliviar a escassez de oferta no curto prazo, enquanto o retorno das chuvas é um bom sinal para a fase de floração, que definirá a safra do próximo ano, afirmaram os corretores. * "Os armazéns (no Brasil) estão se enchendo e as exportações estão ganhando ritmo, afastando as preocupações com os baixos estoques certificados (na bolsa ICE) para cobrir as necessidades de entrega imediata", disse a analista de commodities agrícolas Judy Ganes. * A safra de café do Brasil para 2026/27 deve atingir um recorde de 77,2 milhões de sacas graças às condições climáticas favoráveis, informou a StoneX, elevando sua projeção em 2,6% em relação à estimativa de março. * O café robusta caiu 0,9%, para US$3.374 por tonelada métrica, após atingir a menor cotação em dois meses e meio, de US$3.329. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto fechou em queda de 0,63 centavo, ou 3,4%, a 18,07 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir na quarta-feira seu maior nível desde abril de 2025, a 18,77. * "Não há motivo fundamental para a queda. A retração parece ser mais um movimento de consolidação", disse o analista e consultor de commodities agrícolas Michael McDougall. * Os preços do açúcar estão sendo impulsionados por expectativas generalizadas de um déficit iminente, com a Organização Internacional do Açúcar prevendo um déficit de 300 mil toneladas na safra de 2026/27. * A produção de açúcar no centro-sul do Brasil caiu [USN:L1N44V0UZ TEXT:"7,9%"] em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior no início de agosto, informou o governo. * O açúcar branco caiu 2,3%, para US$526,60 a tonelada. CACAU * O cacau em Londres fechou em baixa de £65, ou 1,4%, a £4.514 por tonelada. O mercado atingiu a maior cotação em um ano, de £4.988, na terça-feira. * A produção de cacau em Gana, segundo maior produtor, deve cair entre 18% e 38% na safra 2026/27 devido ao envelhecimento das árvores, doenças e falhas na polinização, informou a empresa estatal de comercialização de cacau. * O fenômeno climático El Niño também é motivo de preocupação para o cacau. * Por outro lado, no entanto, os amplos estoques globais de cacau devem ajudar a amortecer qualquer impacto na produção causado por condições climáticas adversas, afirmou um executivo da Mondelez International. * O mercado de cacau ainda espera um excedente em 2026/27, embora seja pequeno. * O cacau de Nova York caiu 1,6%, para US$6.174 por tonelada. (Reportagem de May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: US FDA approves Ionis Pharma's therapy to treat rare brain disorder
item.description: The U.S. FDA on Thursday approved Ionis Pharmaceuticals' therapy to treat a rare disease that affects the brain's white matter, making it the first treatment to get the nod for the genetic disorder.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The U.S. FDA on Thursday approved Ionis Pharmaceuticals' (IONS.O) therapy to treat a rare disease that affects the brain's white matter, making it the first treatment to get the nod for the genetic disorder. Ionis' drug zilganersen, branded as Zanvastro, can be used to treat adults and pediatric patients with Alexander disease, a neurological disorder caused by mutations in a gene that can cause seizures and delay physical and intellectual development. The condition affects fewer than 1,000 people in the U.S., according to the National Institutes of Health. In an early-to-late-stage study, patients who got a 50 mg dose of zilganersen showed a statistically significant improvement in gait speed as assessed by a 10-meter walk test, an assessment of functional mobility, at 61 weeks.

item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says Russian drones hit Coca-Cola plant outside Kyiv
item.description: Russian drones struck and damaged a Coca-Cola plant outside the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Thursday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian drones struck and damaged a Coca-Cola (KO.N) plant outside the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Thursday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Officials said there were no injuries in the strike near the town of Brovary, east of the capital. "Today, the Russians have hit a Coca-Cola plant with their drone. Coca-Cola is such an enemy that they set it on fire with their Shaheds," Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address, referring to Iranian-designed drones." "It's a clear Russian signal to America. The Russians cannot be unaware that this is an American facility." Reuters Television footage showed firefighting crews arriving at the scene and smoke rising above the plant and over nearby fields. Andy Hunder, president of the American Chamber of Commerce in Ukraine, said the plant's staff were uninjured. "The company is working with the relevant authorities to assess the situation," Hunder told Reuters. "Ensuring the safety and well-being of people remains top priority."

item.title: Four dead in Ukrainian attack on Russia's border Belgorod region, officials say
item.description: A Ukrainian strike on Thursday killed four people, including two medical personnel, in an attack on Russia's border region of Belgorod, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Ukrainian strike on Thursday killed four people, including two medical personnel, in an attack on Russia's border region of Belgorod, officials said. The region's official headquarters, posting on Telegram, said the dead in Shebekino, just across the border from Ukraine, included a doctor, a medic and a married couple. Three people were injured. The head of Russian-controlled parts of eastern Ukraine's Donetsk Region, meanwhile, said three civilians died in drone strikes in three separate districts of the region.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg had a bold plan to replace Meta staff with AI — and it imploded. Answering readers’ questions on Reddit
item.dc:creator: Katie Paul
item.content:encoded:
To make its workforce "AI native," Meta hatched a radical plan to slash the size of teams across the company by as much as 60% in two waves, known internally as Project OT. But staff revolted and the AI agents did not perform as expected. Hours before a big layoff in May, CEO Mark Zuckerberg called off planning for further cuts. Technology correspondent Katie Paul invited our audience to ask her questions surrounding the fallout. The following questions are from Reddit users, answered by Paul. See the full AMA here:

Hi Reddit, I'm Katie Paul, a Reuters journalist who unveiled Mark Zuckerberg's plan to replace Meta staff with AI — and how it imploded. AMA. by u/reuters in technology

What actually imploded? At most, it seems like a delay. Lots of Meta employees are also wondering if the plan is just on hold. In terms of it imploding, executives have acknowledged some of the problems to employees, and more privately fretted about other aspects of how it went south. For instance, Mark Zuckerberg has talked about getting the timing wrong in one of his internal Q&As with employees, while CTO Andrew Bosworth (known as Boz) said in an internal comment thread that the company did an “atrocious” job explaining the vision. They’ve also expressed concerns about morale, discussed AI’s worrying impact on productivity and site reliability and reversed course on some of the more aggressive AI-forward initiatives. Tokenmaxxing pressure is out — the guidance now is to use AI when it makes sense, not just for the sake of using it. Did Meta plan to substitute employees with AI to save money in a desperate attempt to remain financially afloat? I wouldn’t necessarily use the word “desperate,” but it’s certainly true that Meta is facing a cash crunch in light of its colossal spending on AI infrastructure. This is the explanation Mark Zuckerberg has given employees for the layoffs, as well. He told them in an internal Q&A in late April that the company basically has two cost centers: compute infrastructure and people. If the company is spending more on one, that means it has less capital to allocate to the other, he said. Do you see Meta facing challenges like Amazon did when their AI agents pushed out buggy code into production which wouldn't have happened with a human team? I’m not familiar with what happened at Amazon (will have to ask my colleague about it!), but I can tell you this was definitely happening at Meta. There’s a section in the story about site reliability warning signs flashing due to AI, both in terms of the surge in AI-generated code straining systems and AI agents wreaking havoc. One sign of this was that there were 40% more major site reliability emergencies (called “SEVs” at Meta) taking place compared to last year, and because AI-related events were generally weirder and less predictable compared to human-caused SEVs, staffers were spending 70% more time “firefighting” them. There were various discussions about how to use AI to catch the bugs caused by AI, but at this point that’s a problem people are still trying to solve — at Meta and pretty much everywhere else. Our special report provided the first account of Meta's Project OT — short for Organization Transformation — the social-media giant's ambitious plan to use AI to transform its workforce — and how it stumbled. @katielpaul will answer your questions here ➡️ https://t.co/0do33CMI4O pic.twitter.com/AJ5QfbfnXg — Reuters (@Reuters) September 3, 2026 How did you get wind of the bigger story, and were there any employees who got in trouble for speaking out? Do you think the publicity or internal complaints made them walk it back? As you’ve noted, I have to be VERY careful about what I say on this. What I can tell you is that there were people who thought Meta employees deserved to know what the company was planning — and they thought the wider world deserved to know too, considering how a big overhaul like this could easily become a template replicated widely across the corporate world. I’m grateful to them. I'd like to know more about the angle about the layoffs disproportionately affecting people with disabilities and/or people on medical, parental or other protected types of leave. It wasn't in your article but many others, including at Reuters, have written about it. You and me both! I don’t have specific information on this as it relates to the May 20 layoffs, beyond what’s come out in a lawsuit alleging problems on this front. I’m also familiar with similar allegations related to the company’s drives to push people out via its performance system, which were particularly aggressive last year. Those cases are difficult to track, as staffers are generally bound by the terms of their employment contracts to work out any disputes in private arbitration, and are barred from discussing the outcomes publicly. But it’s a subject that’s very worthy of more reporting. Does Meta fear regulatory backlash from the implications of this story? From the information I have, company leaders are most concerned about the backlash in terms of its impact on morale and future hiring. That may seem counterintuitive for a story about using AI to replace people, but the transformation didn’t go well in a number of different ways, and for now at least Meta needs its employees to get back to the grind. That could change, of course: for instance, Mark Zuckerberg has told staffers that in retrospect he thinks some of what leadership tried to do went too far ahead of where the technology was at this point. But for right now, the company is trying to calm nerves internally by having leaders engage more with staffers, backing off pressure to use AI at every turn and committing not to do any more company-wide layoffs this year. We also know Meta is selectively offering big packages, since lots of employees started looking for other jobs in response to the disruption, and that means the company risks losing some of those “10x” people it wants to keep. In terms of regulation, Meta generally has wide latitude to make business decisions about hiring and firing, especially in the U.S. where employment is “at will.” My colleagues who cover the U.S. regulatory landscape tell me they’re not seeing much real movement afoot to regulate AI-related jobs displacement at this point. That said, there’s a little more action at the state level and in Europe, and Meta has faced at least one notable AI-related lawsuit in response to its May 20 layoffs. My colleague on the employment law beat has written about the many challenges workers face in trying to pursue that kind of case. How Meta navigates this regulatory landscape going forward will be an interesting reporting line to track, especially if the company revives elements of the Project OT plan as the technology improves. Does Meta leadership still believe this plan to be viable in the future? This is a huge open question: Did Meta abandon its plan entirely or just reschedule it? I’m not sure even the company’s leaders have a clear answer on this yet. They’ve told employees repeatedly that they’re operating in a dynamic environment and trying to figure out the best way to structure the company as they go, watching how the technology develops and how the changes they introduce play out. Mark Zuckerberg has also said he’s still optimistic that the path the company charted is the right one broadly speaking and projected that AI models will eventually get good enough to support his vision, maybe within the next three to six months. What I can say for sure is that the Project OT planning process that kicked off early this year is no longer happening. If people are this upset, why are they still using it? Why is Reuters sharing content on these platforms? Does civil disobedience have any meaning in the age of social media when it deals with social media itself? These are keen observations — lots of people in the policy world have been asking similar questions for years now. Some of them have turned to explanations involving possible anticompetitive practices, and it seemed like there was some momentum around that approach for several years, although it’s fizzled now. I can’t speak for Reuters as a whole in terms of where it shares content, but ultimately users and advertisers alike post their stuff where the eyeballs are, and for now, Meta continues to run some of the biggest platforms around. An important question for the company involves how it will continue growing its user base, considering how much of the internet-connected world it’s already signed up and ongoing concerns about youth social media usage. Facilitated by Kate Skelly and Jenna Zucker

item.title: Trump administration takes mail-in ballot fight to US Supreme Court
item.description: In an emergency request, the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to lift Boston-based U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani's order temporarily preventing the USPS from enforcing the new rule.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Chung
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump 's administration asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to let it enforce a new U.S. Postal Service rule tightening the use of mail-in ballots, moving swiftly after a judge temporarily blocked the regulation ahead of November's midterm elections. In an emergency request, the Justice Department asked the Supreme Court to lift Boston-based U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani's order temporarily preventing the USPS from enforcing the new rule, which it adopted following an executive order by the Republican president to restrict mail-in ballots. The USPS regulation would impose new voter-specific data and ballot envelope standards, and potentially refuse the delivery of ballots that do not comply, which critics say could [USN:L1N44T0IL TEXT:"disrupt thousands"] of legitimate votes as the November 3 vote approaches. Republicans are locked in a tight battle to retain control of Congress in the election. Critics say restricting mail-in ballots would stand to disproportionately benefit Republicans given that Democratic voters traditionally have been more likely to use mail-in ballots. It is the second time that the administration has turned to the Supreme Court as it defends Trump's directive against legal challenges by states and voting rights groups. On August 24 the court [USN:S0N41Y01Q TEXT:"lifted"] an earlier injunction imposed by Talwani in June blocking Trump's order. That decision, powered by the court's 6-3 conservative majority, faulted a coalition of mostly Democratic-governed states for suing too soon, but left the door open to another challenge. The court's three liberal justices dissented. RULE WOULD TIGHTEN STANDARDS FOR MAIL BALLOT DELIVERY Under the new USPS rule, states must provide lists of mail ballot recipients to the postal service and use agency-approved outbound and return ballot mail envelopes outfitted with unique barcodes. The postal service could then refuse to send out ballots that do not comply with the new standards or are associated with voters who do not appear on the lists. Trump, who signed his executive order targeting mail-in ballots in March, has for years cast doubt on their security, although evidence of voter fraud is rare. Trump has made false claims of widespread fraud in U.S. elections including his 2020 loss to former Democratic President Joe Biden. The administration in its written filing on Thursday urged the Supreme Court to allow it to implement an "important federal policy to protect the mails from being used to commit voter fraud." A coalition of mostly Democratic-governed states and Washington, D.C., as well as a number of voting rights groups, challenged the new USPS rule. Talwani issued a [USN:L1N44M0T6 TEXT:"temporary order"] on August 27 blocking the rule for 14 days, finding that it likely violates the U.S. Constitution, under which the states administer elections, and would be impossible for the states to comply with given the rapidly approaching midterms. The Justice Department asked the Boston-based 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to put the judge's order on hold, but did not wait for a decision before turning to the Supreme Court. Talwani also held a hearing on Thursday to consider whether to issue a longer-term injunction.

item.title: Sensational Eala basks in fans cheers in second-round win
item.description: Alexandra Eala of the Philippines brushed aside Ukrainian Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-1 6-4 to reach the third round of the U.S. Open on Thursday, keeping the buzz going for her fervent following in New York.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: Alexandra Eala of the Philippines brushed aside Ukrainian Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-1 6-4 to reach the third round of the U.S. Open on Thursday, keeping the buzz going for her fervent following in New York. The 21-year-old lefty lost to Oliynykova in Strasbourg earlier this year but had the right formula this time around as she needed little more than an hour to seal it. She next plays either Iva Jovic of the United States or Briton Francesca Jones. "My patience and the consistency of my focus - I think that was the key to winning the match today," said Eala. Fresh off her career-breakthrough win in D.C. last month, Eala looked poised for a fine run in Flushing Meadows as she won the first four games across a dominant opening set, with 11 winners to none from her opponent. The two traded breaks in a far more competitive second set, where Eala broke her opponent from the baseline in the seventh game before slamming her foot on the gas and clinching it with an unreturnable serve to the delight of the crowd, as the flag of the Philippines dotted the stands. The first player from the Philippines to win a WTA Tour-level match was urged on by her compatriots at Louis Armstrong Stadium, where signs in Tagalog urged her to fight on. "I think we all represent something. I'm proud of what I represent," said Eala.

item.title: Wall Street encerra dia com forte alta, conforme declarações de Waller amenizam temor de elevação dos juros
item.description: Wall Street registrou alta nesta quinta-feira, à medida que os investidores moderaram suas apostas em novos aumentos das taxas de juros, depois que o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller afirmou que apoiaria a manutenção da taxa básica de juros caso os dados indiquem que as pressões inflacionárias estejam diminuindo.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Niket Nishant
item.content:encoded: Wall Street registrou alta nesta quinta-feira, à medida que os investidores moderaram suas apostas em novos aumentos das taxas de juros, depois que o diretor do Federal Reserve Christopher Waller afirmou que apoiaria a manutenção da taxa básica de juros caso os dados indiquem que as pressões inflacionárias estejam diminuindo. Todos os três principais índices acionários dos EUA fecharam com alta de 1% ou mais, com o Nasdaq recebendo um impulso do grupo das “sete magníficas”, formado por ações de megacapitalização relacionadas à inteligência artificial. Todos os três índices estavam a caminho de registrar ganhos semanais. Waller disse à Reuters que estaria inclinado a deixar as taxas de juros de referência inalteradas caso os próximos dados confirmem que as pressões sobre os preços estão diminuindo, mas acrescentou que apoiaria um aumento das taxas caso a inflação não esfrie. Após as declarações de Waller, os mercados financeiros moderaram as expectativas de aumentos das taxas na reunião do Fed em setembro, reduzindo a probabilidade de 63,2% na quarta-feira para 50,4%, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME. O rendimento de referência dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA recuou pela segunda sessão consecutiva, após atingir seu nível mais alto desde novembro de 2023. As expectativas de aumento das taxas haviam disparado nas últimas sessões, à medida que os rendimentos dos títulos de longo prazo subiram para os níveis mais altos em anos, em meio a uma onda global de vendas de títulos impulsionada por temores de inflação, aumento da dívida e incertezas geopolíticas. “Os comentários do diretor do Fed Waller estão proporcionando um impulso generalizado para os mercados como um todo”, disse Bill Northey, diretor sênior de investimentos da U.S. Bank Wealth Management, em Billings, Montana. “Por trás dos índices gerais do mercado, estamos vendo uma influência contínua das empresas que divulgaram seus resultados mais tarde na temporada de divulgação dos lucros do segundo trimestre”, acrescentou Northey. “E isso está gerando alguma diferenciação entre setores como o de chips, onde tivemos um relatório de grande destaque ontem à tarde, e também no setor de software, onde observamos alguns resultados diferenciados, atendendo ou superando padrões um pouco mais baixos.” Os relatórios econômicos desta quinta-feira foram, em geral, otimistas, com baixo número de pedidos de auxílio-desemprego e uma aceleração no setor de serviços. Por outro lado, os dados mostraram que os preços dos insumos no setor de serviços atingiram seu nível mais alto desde outubro de 2022, e o déficit comercial internacional aumentou 24,4%. Na sexta-feira, o Departamento do Trabalho deve divulgar seu relatório de emprego de agosto, que deve mostrar que a economia dos EUA criou 56.000 empregos no mês passado, mantendo a taxa de desemprego estável em 4,1%. O Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) subiu 1,18%, para 53.686,11 pontos, o S&P 500 (.SPX) avançou 1,06%, para 7.747,71 pontos, e o Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) teve alta de 1,40%, para 26.584,06 pontos. Dos 11 principais setores do S&P 500, o de bens de consumo discricionário (.SPLRCD) registrou o maior ganho percentual, enquanto as ações do setor de energia (.SPNY) ficaram para trás. A Nvidia (NVDA.O) subiu 1,8% depois que a empresa anunciou que compraria a plataforma de desenvolvimento Hugging Face por US$12,9 bilhões, em um desafio à OpenAI e à Anthropic. Mas a fabricante de chips Broadcom (AVGO.O) registrou queda de 2,7% após divulgar uma previsão de receita para o quarto trimestre abaixo do esperado, um lembrete de que as empresas no centro da expansão da IA têm um grande desafio a superar. A Snowflake (SNOW.N) disparou 16,6% após prever uma receita anual robusta, impulsionando o otimismo em todo o setor de software. A ServiceNow (NOW.N) , a Salesforce (CRM.N) e a Adobe (ADBE.O) registraram ganhos entre 2,1% e 6,5% no dia. Ações ligadas a criptomoedas subiram depois que o bitcoin se recuperou após duas sessões consecutivas de perdas, com a Strategy (MSTR.O) saltando 17,6% e a Coinbase Global (COIN.O) registrando alta de 10,1%. A plataforma de negociação de varejo Robinhood Markets (HOOD.O) disparou 16,6%.

item.title: Smart ring maker Oura reveals revenue surge in US IPO filing
item.description: Oura, the maker of smart wearable Oura Ring, filed the paperwork for its U.S. initial public offering on Thursday, revealing a revenue surge and adding to a growing list of consumer-focused companies looking to tap public markets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oura, the maker of smart wearable Oura Ring, filed the paperwork for its U.S. initial public offering on Thursday, revealing a revenue surge and adding to a growing list of consumer-focused companies looking to tap public markets. The IPO market is expected to pick up steam after a summer lull. Analysts expect issuers to target the post-Labor Day window to get ahead of any uncertainty around November's midterm elections. Oura, whose journey began more than a decade ago in Oulu, Finland, makes a smart ring that tracks key health indicators such as heart rate, sleep stages and physical activity. The company reported a net income of $60.8 million for the nine months ended June 30, compared with $1.6 million in the same period a year earlier. Revenue jumped 74% to $1.21 billion. Oura has reshaped the wearables industry and grown rapidly in recent years as consumers increasingly embrace smart rings that can provide personalized health insights. In May, it unveiled the fifth generation of its smart ring, which is 40% smaller than the previous version. The firm last year raised over $900 million in a funding led by Fidelity Management & Research Company at a roughly $11 billion valuation. Oura’s original name was Jouzen, based on joutsen, the Finnish word for swan, the country’s national bird. Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, Allen and Co and BofA Securities are among the underwriters for the offering. Oura will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "OURA.”

item.title: Flex to acquire EPC Power in $4.4 billion deal to expand data center power offerings
item.description: Contract manufacturer Flex said on Thursday it will acquire power conversion systems maker EPC Power in a deal valued at $4.4 billion to strengthen its position in AI data center and power infrastructure markets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Contract manufacturer Flex (FLEX.O) said on Thursday it will acquire power conversion systems maker EPC Power in a deal valued at $4.4 billion to strengthen its position in AI data center and power infrastructure markets. Here are more details: Flex said the deal will expand its Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) business as demand for AI infrastructure and next-generation 800V data center power systems grows. Flex CEO Revathi Advaithi said EPC Power's power conversion and grid-forming technology will help Flex benefit from the shift to next-generation power systems. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, after which EPC Power will become part of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure (CPI) segment. Flex said it intends to separate its CPI segment into a standalone public company in the first quarter of 2027. Flex said it expects to finance the acquisition through a combination of debt and equity, with committed financing provided by Citi and Bank of America. EPC Power develops power conversion systems used in data centers, energy storage projects and electric grids. The company has deployed more than 15 gigawatts of power systems in 62 countries and expects its U.S. manufacturing capacity to exceed 30 gigawatts in 2027.

item.title: Vídeo de discussão entre Moraes e Mendonça no STF é de 2023
item.description: Um vídeo de uma discussão entre os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), é de 2023, mas posts tratam o registro como se fosse desta semana, após Mendonça retirar o sigilo de mensagens do ex-dono do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, para Moraes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo de uma discussão entre os ministros Alexandre de Moraes e André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), é de 2023, mas posts tratam o registro como se fosse desta semana, após Mendonça retirar o sigilo de mensagens do ex-dono do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, para Moraes. Aqui estão os principais detalhes: Publicações no Instagram alegam que o bate-boca aconteceu nesta terça-feira, “no mesmo dia em que vieram à tona mensagens trocadas entre Moraes e Daniel Vorcaro”. No vídeo, Moraes afirma que o colega sugere a existência de uma conspiração do “governo contra o próprio governo”, e Mendonça responde dizendo “não coloque palavras na minha boca”. O diálogo ocorreu em setembro de 2023, durante o julgamento de um dos réus dos ataques às sedes dos Três Poderes em 8 de janeiro daquele ano, como confirma a transmissão da sessão publicada pelo STF em seu canal no YouTube. As cenas, portanto, foram registradas quase três anos antes de Mendonça, relator do inquérito que investiga o Banco Master no STF, levantar o sigilo de um relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) com mensagens enviadas por Vorcaro a Moraes. VEREDICTO: Legenda errada. O vídeo mostra uma discussão entre Moraes e Mendonça em 2023, não recentemente. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check.
